newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA WIN SECOND MATCH UNDER VENABLES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA WIN SECOND MATCH UNDER VENABLES.

text.p: Australia won their second match in four days at the start of Terry Venables' era as national coach with a 2-1 victory over 10-man South Korea in a four-nation tournament on Wednesday.
Fullback Matthew Bingley and substitute striker Alistair Edwards scored in each half at Lang Park to give Australia their first success against South Korea in more than a decade.
South Korea played all but one minute of the second half with only ten men after fullback Kim Sang Hoon was sent off for his second bookable offence.
Midfielder Ha Seok Ju scored a consolation for the visitors with a direct free-kick in the 76th minute.
"It's early days yet, but I'm really pleased with the team's performance tonight. We created chances and we defended well against a very good side," Venables said.
"We've only had four training sessions together and I thought we did a lot of things better."

Australia lead the tournament with six points from two games, three points clear of South Korea and Norway, who beat New Zealand 3-0 in Wednesday's other match. New Zealand prop up the table without a point.
Australia must win the Oceania qualifying group before a play-off against the fourth-best Asian side to earn a place at next year's World Cup.
"That is the sort of test we will face if we want to get to the World Cup," said Venables, who signed an 18-month contract to lead Australia in their campaign to qualify for the finals in France.
Kim was booked for a clumsy challenge on Australia midfielder Craig Foster before being dismissed in the 46th minute for failing to retreat 10 yards at a free-kick.

Bingley, who scored Australia's only goal against New Zealand in Melbourne on Saturday, slotted the ball home from close range in the 37th minute amid South Korean protests that the ball had gone out of play earlier in the move.
After Kim's dismissal, Australia exploited the extra space, leaving Edwards free in front of goal and he hammered the ball past Kim Byung Ji in the 72nd minute.
Australia will play Norway while South Korea take on New Zealand in the final round of matches in Sydney on Saturday.
